anshul: small follow-up after the rfc: should tenant pins support selector patterns (family/semver) or only exact content-hash?

vivian: UX favors patterns. ops needs control though. propose explicit modes: hard=exact, soft=family auto-patch, gated=family but require approval on breaking diffs.

joel: main infra risks: nondeterministic routing if family maps to multiple hashes and extra index lookups per request. we should cache family->hash and emit the resolved hash in telemetry.

carla: schema suggestion (flat fields): pin_scope, selector_type, selector_value, pin_mode, fallback_strategy, resolution_ttl, require_resolution_audit. example as code block in PR: ```json
{
  "pin_scope": "tenant",
  "selector_type": "family",
  "selector_value": "luma-3.1",
  "pin_mode": "soft",
  "fallback_strategy": "prefer_exact",
  "resolution_ttl": "300s",
  "require_resolution_audit": "true"
}```

anshul: agree. migration note: existing tenant pins default to hard/exact. also add `resolution_eligibility` to opt-out of auto-patch for sensitive tenants.

joel: infra ticket INF-7234 created for etag index + family->hash webhook for Dedicated. caching strategy: watch events + small in-memory LRU to keep O(1) resolution. also define deterministic tie-breaker for multi-hash families (stable weight then creation_time).

infra-bot: INF-7234 logged.

anshul: action items: 1) carla open schema PR with examples + migration playbook. 2) joel spec cache/telemetry events (family_resolution, fallback_applied). 3) vivian draft customer migration notes. i'll link RFC + PR.

carla: i'll include curl and SDK snippets for hard/soft/gated flows and example responses showing resolved hash when require_resolution_audit=true.

sam: sounds good. make sure Dedicated and Private customers get the webhook docs. :thumbsup:
